title: Carotid Artery Cannulation in Mice
author: Jason Kim
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x4pfqvn

steps.title: Anesthetize the mice
steps.instruction: Administer anesthesia via intraperitoneal injection and verify the depth of anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Inject ketamine (100 mg/kg body weight) and xylazine (10 mg/kg body weight) intraperitoneally.
Check the level of general anesthesia using a pinch stimulus of the animal's tail and/or foot.

steps.title: Isolate the carotid artery
steps.instruction: Expose the carotid artery by making a transverse incision (~0.5 cm) over the trachea.

steps.title: Insert the catheter
steps.instruction: Introduce a silastic catheter (PE 10) into the vessel.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the catheter is filled with a saline solution containing heparin (10 U/ml) and plugged before introduction.

steps.title: Secure the catheter
steps.instruction: Route the catheter to the back of the neck and secure it for future access.

substeps.instruction: Guide the catheter to the back of the neck and place it under the back skin.
Tie a silk to the catheter.
Make a small opening at the back of the neck to leave the silk partially exposed for pulling on the day of the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare catheter for experiment
steps.instruction: On the day of the experiment, flush the catheter using a heparinised saline solution.
